contract: Each caller owns only its wait. Cancelling one waiter must not cancel a shared operation while any other waiter remains active. Once the last waiter cancels, transport cancellation is required. Completed responses settle active waiters only.

evidenceRequirements.description: Explain how the supplied guard preserves its contract across relevant ownership/time boundaries. Do not require knowledge of an unseen sibling. Evaluator counterfactual only: Two callers join one lookup; caller a cancels and is removed. Unconditional abort cancels the transport even though b remains. Later completion rejects b as cancelled instead of delivering its result. Reference-counted cancellation preserves b and still aborts when the last waiter leaves.

Explain at least one relevant boundary or benign path inferable from the supplied code/context; the following evaluator examples are alternatives, not a mandatory unseen checklist: Last-waiter cancellation still aborts; cancelling twice is idempotent; another key is unaffected; completion after one cancellation delivers only to the remaining waiter.

forbiddenClaims: Production outage, real data exfiltration or universal safety without supplied evidence.
A missing contract establishes either a definite defect or unconditional protection.
Simulated time or offline passing tests establish real scheduler/OS behavior or model improvement.
